sentences.zh: 他曾与斯坦利、亨利·莫顿·斯坦利一起去救援埃及。

sentences.en: It's such a complicated story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常复杂的故事。

sentences.en: Basically, they went to rescue an Egyptian governor called Emin Pasha, who didn't need rescuing in the Sudan.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们去苏丹是为了救援一个名叫埃明·帕夏的埃及总督，而根本不需要救援。

sentences.en: And this guy, Bartolot, behaved, it's fair to say, very poorly.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，这个叫巴托洛特的家伙表现非常糟糕。

sentences.en: He went mad.
sentences.zh: 他疯了。

sentences.en: He started flogging people wildly.
sentences.zh: 他开始疯狂地鞭打别人。

sentences.en: He put loads of people in chains and he started running around biting women.
sentences.zh: 他把许多人用铁链锁起来，还开始四处乱咬女人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Very bad behavior.
sentences.zh: 非常糟糕的行为。

sentences.en: And eventually, this African bloke shot him dead.
sentences.zh: 最终，一个非洲本地人一枪打死了他。

sentences.en: And that was the end of him.
sentences.zh: 他的一生就这样结束了。

sentences.en: And everyone said, God almighty, what a terrible advert for Britain.
sentences.zh: 每个人都说，天哪，这是英国多么糟糕的宣传广告啊。

sentences.en: Let's never speak of this again.
sentences.zh: 让我们再也不要提这件事了。

sentences.en: So there's that guy, Bartolot.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那个叫巴托洛特的家伙。

sentences.en: He possibly is an inspiration for Kurtz.
sentences.zh: 他很可能是库尔茨的灵感来源之一。

sentences.en: Then there's a Belgian called Arthur Hoddister.
sentences.zh: 然后是一个叫亚瑟·霍迪斯特的比利时人。

sentences.en: Strange name for a Belgian, I always think, but there you go.
sentences.zh: 我总觉得对于一个比利时人来说这是一个奇怪的名字，但事实就是如此。

sentences.en: He was an ivory trader and was brilliant at it, like Kurtz.
sentences.zh: 他是一个象牙商人，而且在这方面非常出色，就像库尔茨一样。

sentences.en: He was ruthless.
sentences.zh: 他冷酷无情。

sentences.en: He had a harem of local women.
sentences.zh: 他有一群当地女性组成的妻妾。

sentences.en: There were rumors that local people worshipped him as a god.
sentences.zh: 有传言说当地人把他当成神一样崇拜。

sentences.en: But he came to a very different end from Kurtz.
sentences.zh: 但他迎来了与库尔茨截然不同的结局。

sentences.en: He was tortured, beheaded.
sentences.zh: 他遭受了酷刑，被斩首。

sentences.en: And according to some accounts, eaten by Swahili slave traders for kind of intruding on their patch.
sentences.zh: 根据某些记载，他因为侵入了斯瓦希里奴隶贩子的地盘，而被他们吃掉了。

sentences.en: That would have been a good end to Heart of Darkness.
sentences.zh: 那将是《黑暗的心》的一个好结局。

sentences.en: It would have been an unexpected end.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个意想不到的结局。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Then there's a guy called Carl Peters who was a German.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一个叫卡尔·彼得斯的德国人。

sentences.en: He was basically Germany's answer to Henry Morton Stanley.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是德国版的亨利·莫顿·斯坦利。

sentences.en: He launched his own expedition to rescue this bloke him in Pasha who didn't need rescuing.
sentences.zh: 他发起自己的远征去救援这个并不需要救援的埃明·帕夏。

sentences.en: He discovered ancient sites along the Zambezi River.
sentences.zh: 他在赞比西河沿岸发现了古代遗址。

sentences.en: He's basically got a bit of the Indiana Jones.
sentences.zh: 他基本上有点印第安纳·琼斯的风范。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, even Germans were embarrassed by this bloke.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，连德国人都为这家伙感到尴尬。

sentences.en: He also went a bit mad.
sentences.zh: 他也变得有点疯狂。

sentences.en: He was incredibly violent.
sentences.zh: 他极其暴力。

sentences.en: His nickname was Hangman Peters because basically, you know, you said good morning to him and he hanged you.
sentences.zh: 他的外号叫绞刑架彼得斯，因为基本上，你知道的，你跟他道个早安他就能把你吊死。

sentences.en: He was very violent.
sentences.zh: 他非常暴力。

sentences.en: And even the Germans who were behaving quite badly, it's fair to say, or indeed very badly in southwest Africa at this point, even they're ashamed of him,
sentences.zh: 甚至连那些当时表现得相当糟糕——或者确实非常糟糕（在西南非洲）的德国人都为他感到羞耻，

sentences.en: which tells his own story.
sentences.zh: 这本身就说明了问题。

sentences.en: And then the final candidate, which Adam Hochschild mentions in his book, King Leopold's Ghost, is a guy called Leon Rom.
sentences.zh: 最后一个候选人是亚当·霍克希尔德在他的书《利奥波德国王的鬼魂》中提到的，一个叫莱昂·罗姆的家伙。

sentences.en: Rom was a Belgian.
sentences.zh: 罗姆是个比利时人。

sentences.en: He was a captain in the Force Publique.
sentences.zh: 他是刚果公共军的一名上尉。

sentences.en: Like Kurtz, he liked painting and writing and he collected butterflies, which is nice, like Vladimir Nabokov.
sentences.zh: 就像库尔茨一样，他喜欢画画和写作，他还收集蝴蝶，这很好，就像弗拉基米尔·纳博科夫一样。

sentences.en: And Maximilian.
sentences.zh: 还有马克西米利安。

sentences.en: The Emperor Maximilian of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥皇帝马克西米利安。

sentences.en: But also he was an obsessive hunter.
sentences.zh: 但同时他也是个着迷的猎手。

sentences.en: He had loads of African concubines.
sentences.zh: 他有成群的非洲妾室。

sentences.en: He had, at the time, and I quote, the reputation of having killed masses of people for petty reasons.
sentences.zh: 当时他甚至有——我引述一下——因琐事而残杀无数平民的恶名。

sentences.en: And he kept a flower bed at his station ringed with human heads.
sentences.zh: 而且他的驻地用一圈人头围成了一个花坛。

sentences.en: Oh, that's very Kurtz.
sentences.zh: 哦，这太库尔茨了。

sentences.en: Which is very Kurtz.
sentences.zh: 确实非常库尔茨。

sentences.en: So, as Jiswath Nydas says in his biography of Conrad, Conrad may well have drawn on all these examples, but it's clear that Kurtz is all of them and none of them.
sentences.zh: 因此，正如伊斯沃思·奈达在康拉德传记中所说，康拉德很可能借鉴了所有这些例子，但显而易见的是，库尔茨既是所有人，又谁都不是。

sentences.en: As Nydas says, the model for Kurtz comes from literary and philosophical tradition as much as it does from real life African behaviour.
sentences.zh: 正如奈达所说，库尔茨的原型既源自文学和哲学传统，也源自现实生活中的非洲行为。

sentences.en: Well, there's the quality of the Byronic hero.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里有一种拜伦式英雄的特质。

sentences.en: The man who is elevated by the terrible knowledge that he has won from experience.
sentences.zh: 那种从亲身经历的残酷教训中获得觉悟而变得高大的人。

sentences.en: I mean, it's definitely a kind of literary trope.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对是一种文学套路。

sentences.en: You mentioned what I think is the obvious thing, which is FauSt.
sentences.zh: 你提到了我认为显而易见的一点，那就是《浮士德》。

sentences.en: So, Faust has sold his soul to the devil.
sentences.zh: 所以，浮士德把灵魂卖给了魔鬼。

sentences.en: And it's not just Marlow, but obviously Goethe wrote about FauSt.
sentences.zh: 不仅是马洛，显然歌德也写过《浮士德》。

sentences.en: And then Thomas Mann will write about Faust a few decades after Conrad.
sentences.zh: 然后在康拉德之后的几十年里，托马斯·曼也将书写浮士德。

sentences.en: And there are a few references Marlow says at one point in Heart of Darkness, Kurtz has taken a high seat among the devils of the land.
sentences.zh: 马洛在《黑暗的心》中某处有过几次提及，他说库尔茨在当地恶魔中占据了高位。

sentences.en: And later on, he talks about how the powers of darkness are about to claim him for their own.
sentences.zh: 后来，他谈到黑暗势力如何即将把库尔茨据为己有。

sentences.en: So, this idea that Kurtz has sold his soul to the devil, you know, it's a very old idea and kind of European.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种库尔茨将灵魂出卖给魔鬼的想法，你知道的，是一个非常古老且带点欧洲色彩的概念。

sentences.en: But there's also something new about Kurtz.
sentences.zh: 但库尔茨身上也有某种新颖的东西。

sentences.en: He's the embodiment of progress.
sentences.zh: 他是进步的化身。

sentences.en: Remember that he's so talented.
sentences.zh: 别忘了他是如此才华横溢。

sentences.en: He's the epitome.
sentences.zh: 他是个典范。

sentences.en: He's the embodiment of civilisation.
sentences.zh: 他是文明的化身。

sentences.en: And there is an argument, I think, that what he's doing in that long...
sentences.zh: 而且有一种观点认为，他在那篇长文中所做的事……

sentences.en: Remember, he writes that very long report.
sentences.zh: 记住，他写了那份极长的报告。

sentences.en: Yeah, so exterminate all the brutes.
sentences.zh: 对，也就是“消灭所有野蛮人”。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's an argument that that report is in itself the embodiment of the European project in Africa to categorise, to set down on, to turn everything into accounts and ledgers.
sentences.zh: 有一种观点认为，那份报告本身就是欧洲在非洲计划的缩影：将一切分类、记录，把万物变成账目和总账。

sentences.en: Which began with Napoleon going to Egypt.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于拿破仑远征埃及。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: To put Africa down on paper and control it and map it.
sentences.zh: 把非洲记录在纸面上，加以控制并绘制地图。

sentences.en: Very Edward Said.
sentences.zh: 非常爱德华·萨义德。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That is the act of colonialism, effectively.
sentences.zh: 这实际上就是殖民主义的行为。

sentences.en: Well, European colonialism.
sentences.zh: 嗯，欧洲殖民主义。

sentences.en: European colonialism.
sentences.zh: 欧洲殖民主义。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So is this, therefore, a story about colonialism and is Kurtz the embodiment of all that's wrong with it?
sentences.zh: 那么，这到底是一个关于殖民主义的故事，而库尔茨是其中一切弊病的化身吗？

sentences.en: At one level, I think the answer is obviously yes.
sentences.zh: 在某种层面上，我认为答案显然是肯定的。

sentences.en: Marlowe, at the beginning, is given those lines about taking the earth away from people with flatter noses than ourselves that are kind of very pointed.
sentences.zh: 马洛在开篇时说的那些关于“从鼻子比我们扁平的人手中夺走土地”的台词，可以说是相当一针见血。

sentences.en: Later on in the book, only a little bit later, before Marlowe actually goes to the Congo, he goes to visit his aunt.
sentences.zh: 在书的后面，没过多久，在马洛真正去刚果之前，他去拜访了他的姑妈。

sentences.en: And his aunt has been reading newspaper stories about Africa and empire.
sentences.zh: 他的姑妈一直在读关于非洲和帝国的报纸报道。

sentences.en: And she says, oh, it's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 她说，哦，这太棒了。

sentences.en: Love this project.
sentences.zh: 太喜欢这个计划了。

sentences.en: Weaning those ignorant millions from their horrid ways.
sentences.zh: 把那些愚昧的数百万民众从可怕的习俗中拯救出来。

sentences.en: And Marlowe actually says to her, this is even before he's gone.
sentences.zh: 而马洛实际上对她说了——甚至在他动身之前——

sentences.en: He says, it's about money.
sentences.zh: 他说，这全是为了钱。

sentences.en: The company is run for profit.
sentences.zh: 这家公司是为了谋取利润而运营的。

sentences.en: You know, he's unsentimental about what is motivating all this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他对这一切的动机毫无温情脉脉的幻想。

sentences.en: And of course, then when he gets to the Congo, everything that he sees could come from a charge sheet about the crimes of empire.
sentences.zh: 当然，当他到达刚果时，他所看到的一切都可以直接写进一份帝国罪行的起诉书。

sentences.en: The skulls, the skeletons, you know, the violence, all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 头骨、骨架，你知道的，暴力，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the things that strikes me about it, a bit like War of the Worlds, where Wells transposes the horrors of European colonialism to Britain.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，其中一件事让我印象深刻，有点像《世界大战》，儒勒·凡尔纳把欧洲殖民主义的恐怖搬到了英国。

sentences.en: There's a sense that occasionally that Conrad is doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得康拉德偶尔也在做同样的事情。

sentences.en: So the whole, the opening with Britain as Africa.
sentences.zh: 所以整本书的开篇，是将英国视作非洲。

sentences.en: But also there's a kind of an amazing passage.
sentences.zh: 但这里还有一个令人惊叹的片段。

sentences.en: So he's looking out at, Marlowe is looking out at all the villages that are abandoned.
sentences.zh: 马洛正望着外面那些被废弃的村庄。

sentences.en: And he says, well, you know, if loads of Africans suddenly, you know, armed with terrifying weapons,
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，你知道的，如果大批非洲人突然——你知道的，手持可怕的武器——

sentences.en: started appearing on the road that stretches between Deal and Gravesend in Kent, catching the yokels right and left to carry heavy loads for them.
sentences.zh: 开始出现在肯特郡迪尔和格雷夫森德之间的公路上，左右抓捕当地乡巴佬为他们运送重物，

sentences.en: I fancy every farm and cottage thereabouts would get empty very soon.
sentences.zh: 我猜那里的每个农场和村舍很快就会空无一人。

sentences.en: And of course, that is a prefiguring of the slave labour in due course that the Nazis will introduce in the heart of Europe.
sentences.zh: 当然，这正是纳粹日后将在欧洲腹地引入的奴隶劳工的预兆。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这完全正确。

sentences.en: And I think the beginning of the book, by transposing what happens to Britain, it makes it very obvious that Conrad is conscious that this has a wider implication.
sentences.zh: 我认为这本书的开篇通过置换发生在英国的场景，非常明显地表明康拉德意识到这具有更广泛的含义。

sentences.en: This is kind of universal message.
sentences.zh: 这是一种普遍的信息。

sentences.en: But here's the complication within the complication.
sentences.zh: 但复杂之处套着复杂之处，这里是这样的。

sentences.en: The framing narrator is very keen on the British Empire, because while he's at Gravesend, he muses on the night errants of the sea, bearers of a spark from the sacred fire,
sentences.zh: 引子里的叙述者对大英帝国非常热心，因为当他在格雷夫森德时，他沉思着海上的流浪骑士、圣火火种的传递者、

sentences.en: the dreams of men, the seed of commonwealth, the germ of empires.
sentences.zh: 人类的梦想、英联邦的种子、帝国的萌芽。

sentences.en: People have sailed out from here with a spark of Britishness.
sentences.zh: 人们带着英国性的小火花从这里扬帆起航。

sentences.en: And isn't that brilliant?
sentences.zh: 这难道不是很棒吗？

sentences.en: Marlowe, the other narrator, he also thinks the British Empire is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 马洛，另一个叙述者，他也认为大英帝国棒极了。

sentences.en: He says at one point he sees a map with a lot of Africa splashed with British imperial pink or red.
sentences.zh: 他有一次说他看到一张地图，上面大部分非洲涂上了大英帝国的粉红色或红色。

sentences.en: And he said, oh, that's good to see, because one knows that real work is being done there, i.e. the British Empire is different from other empires.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，很高兴看到这一点，因为人们知道那里正在进行真正的伟业，也就是说大英帝国与其他帝国不同。

sentences.en: So very Kipling.
sentences.zh: 非常有吉卜林的风格。

sentences.en: But we know that Conrad himself thought that.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道康拉德本人也是这么想的。

sentences.en: So just after he's finished Heart of Darkness, the Burr War breaks out and his Polish relatives say to him, what do you make of this?
sentences.zh: 就在他刚写完《黑暗的心》之后，布尔战争爆发了，他的波兰亲戚对他说，你怎么看这件事？

sentences.en: You know, an empire against a little people at the Burrs?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，一个帝国对抗布尔人这样一个弱小民族？

sentences.en: You know, it doesn't ring any bells.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这难道没让你联想到什么吗？

sentences.en: And he says, well, the British are brilliant.
sentences.zh: 而他说，好吧，英国人太棒了。

sentences.en: Liberty can only be found under the English flag all over the world.
sentences.zh: 自由只能在世界各地飘扬的英国国旗下找到。

sentences.en: So he's for the Burr War.
sentences.zh: 所以他是支持布尔战争的。

sentences.en: And then after he died, his great friend and collaborator, Ford Mannix Ford, said of him a line that always amuses me, the British Empire was for Conrad,
sentences.zh: 在他死后，他的挚友兼合作者福特·马多克斯·福特曾对他说过一句总是让我忍俊不禁的话：大英帝国对康拉德而言，

sentences.en: the perfection of all human perfections.
sentences.zh: 是所有人类完美之中的完美。

sentences.en: So Conrad, obviously, a brilliant judge of empires.
sentences.zh: 所以康拉德显然是个绝佳的帝国裁判官。

sentences.en: But this has led some people to say, well, hold on, you know, you can't celebrate this book as a criticism of empire.
sentences.zh: 但这导致一些人说，等等，你知道的，你不能把这本书当作对帝国的批判来赞美。

sentences.en: In fact, let's go further.
sentences.zh: 事实上，让我们说得更远一点。

sentences.en: This book is itself massively tainted with the crimes of empire.
sentences.zh: 这本书本身就深深地沾染了帝国的罪行。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a it's a tainted example of imperialist literature.
sentences.zh: 这是一个被玷污了的帝国主义文学样本。

sentences.en: Although, if you read it and you didn't know about Conrad's enthusiasm for British imperialism, would you necessarily recognize that?
sentences.zh: 尽管如果你读了它，却不知道康拉德对英国帝国主义的热情，你还能必然地认出这一点吗？

sentences.en: Well, there are at least two critics who think you would.
sentences.zh: 好吧，至少有两位评论家认为你能。

sentences.en: So one of them, I think you mentioned him already, didn't you?
sentences.zh: 其中一位，我想你已经提过他了吧？

sentences.en: Edward Said, Palestinian American critic, one of the most famous literary critics of the last half century, who wrote a brilliantly influential book, shall we say,
sentences.zh: 爱德华·萨义德，巴勒斯坦裔美国评论家，过去半个世纪中最著名的文学评论家之一，他写了一本具有巨大影响力的书，姑且这么说吧，

sentences.en: called Orientalism, which some scholars think is a terrible book.
sentences.zh: 名叫《东方主义》，一些学者认为这是一本糟糕透顶的书。

sentences.en: I think it's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 我认为它太棒了。

sentences.en: I think you said it's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 我想你说过它很棒。

sentences.en: Anyway, Said says, yes, you would recognize Conrad's as an imperialist because he doesn't ever reject imperialism in his book.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，萨义德说，是的，你会把康拉德认作一个帝国主义者，因为他在书中从未拒绝过帝国主义。

sentences.en: He doesn't give the, you know, his book should end with people being given their freedom or some savage critique of the imperialism that has enslaved them.
sentences.zh: 他没有给出——你知道的，他的书本该以人们重获自由或是对奴役他们的帝国主义进行猛烈批判而告终。

sentences.en: I mean, that is what you get.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那才是你应该得到的。

sentences.en: That is what you get.
sentences.zh: 那才是你应该得到的。

sentences.en: Well, a savage critique.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一场猛烈的批判。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, maybe it's not a savage enough for Edward Said.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许对爱德华·萨义德来说还不够猛烈。

sentences.en: Indeed, and Edward Said is also really disappointed that Conrad doesn't give the Africans a chance of redemption or a chance of escape.
sentences.zh: 确实，而且爱德华·萨义德也确实对康拉德没有给非洲人一个救赎或逃脱的机会感到失望。

sentences.en: And I mentioned in the essay by David Demby of The New Yorker, he had a little passage in this essay in 1995, imagining saying, well, how would that work?
sentences.zh: 我在《纽约客》的大卫·登比的文章中提到过，他在1995年这篇文章的一个小片段中，设想并说道，那会是怎样的情景？

sentences.en: Like at the end of the book, you know, Kurt rises from his deathbed and says to an African chief,
sentences.zh: 就像在书的结尾，你知道的，库尔茨从病榻上坐起来，对一个非洲酋长说，

sentences.en: one day your people will be free and the clouds clear and the sun shines and everybody's singing and dancing.
sentences.zh: 有一天你们的人民会获得自由，乌云散去，阳光普照，每个人都在载歌载舞。

sentences.en: It'd be ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 那太荒谬了。

sentences.en: But that's why Said is a brilliant cultural critic, but he's, you know, he never writes a great work of literature because it would simply be agitprop.
sentences.zh: 但这就是为什么萨义德是一位杰出的文化评论家，但他——你知道的——永远写不出伟大的文学作品，因为它纯粹会变成宣传喉舌。

sentences.en: Conrad's story is vastly more complex and unsettling than a kind of programmatic response to this would demand.
sentences.zh: 康拉德的故事要远比这种程式化的回应所要求的复杂和令人不安得多。

sentences.en: I totally agree with you about that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，关于这一点我完全赞同你的看法。

sentences.en: But there's a more substantial critique.
sentences.zh: 但还有一个更有分量的批判。

sentences.en: Now, this is by an African writer called Chinua Achebe.
sentences.zh: 这个批判来自一位名叫钦努阿·阿契贝的非洲作家。

sentences.en: So Nigerian, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他是尼日利亚人吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, born in 1930.
sentences.zh: 对，1930年出生。

sentences.en: And in 1975, Achebe gave this lecture at the University of Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 在1975年，阿契贝在马萨诸塞大学发表了这篇演讲。

sentences.en: To people who don't know, this will sound like such a trivial and footling thing,
sentences.zh: 对于不了解的人来说，这听起来会是一件微不足道且琐碎的小事，

sentences.en: but this is one of the most influential lectures ever given about kind of about literary culture at all.
sentences.zh: 但这是关于文学文化有史以来最具影响力的演讲之一。

sentences.en: It's one of the great demolition jobs, and it's actually a foundational moment for what's called post-colonial literary studies.
sentences.zh: 这是最精彩的批判颠覆之一，它实际上是所谓后殖民文学研究的奠基时刻。

sentences.en: And Achebe said, this is, I hate this book.
sentences.zh: 阿契贝说，这就是，我讨厌这本书。

sentences.en: I hate Conrad and I hate this book, basically because he just sets up Africa as the heart of darkness.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌康拉德，我也讨厌这本书，基本上是因为他把非洲设定为黑暗的心脏。

sentences.en: It's the place where Europeans go to find the evil within themselves.
sentences.zh: 那是欧洲人去寻找内心邪恶的地方。

sentences.en: You know, Conrad's message is keep away from Africa or else.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，康拉德传达的信息是：离非洲远点，否则后果自负。

sentences.en: You know, you'll fall victim to the allure of the jungle.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你会沦为丛林诱惑的牺牲品。

sentences.en: The darkness will find you out.
sentences.zh: 黑暗会找到你的。

sentences.en: You know, you'll become evil if you go to Africa.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你去了非洲，你就会变邪恶。

sentences.en: And he said, and I'm going to quote him, the point of my observation should be quite clear by now, namely that Joseph Conrad was a thoroughgoing raciSt.
sentences.zh: 他说——我引用他的话——我这番观察的重点到现在应该很清楚了，那就是约瑟夫·康拉德是一个彻头彻尾的种族主义者。

sentences.en: And he goes on to say, can a book which dehumanizes Africans, which treats Africa as the heart of darkness, et cetera, et cetera, can it be called a great work of art?
sentences.zh: 他接着说，一本将非洲人非人化、将非洲视为黑暗心脏等的书，能被称为伟大的艺术作品吗？

sentences.en: My answer is, no, it cannot.
sentences.zh: 我的回答是，不，不能。

sentences.en: And this has always been incredibly contentious, this argument among scholars and enthusiasts for Joseph Conrad.
sentences.zh: 在学者和约瑟夫·康拉德的拥趸之间，这个论点一直极具争议。

sentences.en: You know, is this basically a racist book?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这基本上是一本种族主义书籍吗？

sentences.en: And now on college campuses, you will find a lot of people who say it is and either don't teach it or who teach it as an example of literary racism.
sentences.zh: 现在在大学校园里，你会发现很多人认为它是，要么不教这本书，要么把它作为文学种族主义的例子来教。

sentences.en: Now, a lot of people listening to this will expect, because with the rest is history, that at this point we kind of turn our guns on Chinua and Chaby and say, this is terrible,
sentences.zh: 现在，许多收听节目的听众会预料到，因为这是“历史的其余部分”，此时我们会把枪口对准钦努阿·阿契贝，然后说这太糟糕了，

sentences.en: Conrad's brilliant, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 康拉德太棒了，巴拉巴拉。

sentences.en: Actually, there are elements of his critique, I don't know what you think, Tom, but that I think are justified.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他的批判中有些部分——汤姆，我不知道你怎么想——我认为是合情合理的。

sentences.en: So, first of all, he does present, the book does present Africa as primeval, as unfathomable, as prehistoric.
sentences.zh: 首先，这本书确实把非洲呈现为原始的、深不可测的、史前的地方。

sentences.en: Going up that river was like travelling back to the earliest beginnings of the world, when vegetation rioted on the earth and the big trees were kings.
sentences.zh: 逆流而上就像是回到了世界最早的初期，当时植物在大地上肆意疯长，参天大树犹如君王。

sentences.en: Okay, I accept that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我接受这一点。

sentences.en: However, one of the reasons why it is travelling back to the earliest beginnings of the world is that there are no humans,
sentences.zh: 然而，之所以这是一场回到世界初期的旅行，原因之一是那里没有人类，

sentences.en: and there are no humans there because they've all been scared off by the depredations of European colonialists.
sentences.zh: 那里没有人类，是因为他们都被欧洲殖民主义者的掠夺吓跑了。

sentences.en: So, he's not simply saying, you know, the silent, what is it, he says, an empty stream, a great silence.
sentences.zh: 所以，他并不仅仅是在说，你知道的，那死寂的——他是怎么说的——一条空旷的河流，一片巨大的寂静。

sentences.en: That great silence is expressive of the depredations of European colonists.
sentences.zh: 那巨大的寂静正是欧洲殖民者掠夺行为的表露。

sentences.en: I agree with you, but you might not know that reading Conrad's book.
sentences.zh: 我同意你的看法，但读康拉德的书时你可能未必能体会到这一点。

sentences.en: Well, he does, he said it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他的确写了，他说了。

sentences.en: I mean, we just quoted the stuff about, you know, the Africans turning up in Kent and launching attacks.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们刚引用了关于非洲人出现在肯特郡并发起袭击的那段话。

sentences.en: Yes, I suppose so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想也是。

sentences.en: But those two passages are quite far apart, and you might not draw the connection.
sentences.zh: 但那两段相距甚远，你可能不会把它们联系起来。

sentences.en: But that is why Conrad is a great writer, because he's setting up these, you know, these echoes in the prose that reverberate.
sentences.zh: 但这就是为什么康拉德是一位伟大的作家，因为他在散文中营造了这些不断回响的共鸣。

sentences.en: Now, the second charge, I think slightly harder to quibble with, I would argue, is that this is a book about Africa that has no serious African characters at all.
sentences.zh: 现在，第二项指控，我认为稍微更难反驳，那就是这是一本完全没有严肃非洲角色的关于非洲的书。

sentences.en: And when they speak, they don't speak.
sentences.zh: 当他们说话时，他们并没有在说话。

sentences.en: They chant, they grunt, they make, and I quote,
sentences.zh: 他们在吟唱，在咕哝，他们发出——我引述一下——

sentences.en: a drone of weird incantations, strings of amazing words that resembled no sounds of human language, like the responses of some satanic litany.
sentences.zh: 一种怪异的咒语般的嗡嗡声，一串串惊人的词语，听起来不像是人类语言的任何声音，就像某种撒旦式连祷的应答。

sentences.en: And even the physical descriptions that are quite harrowing, they're quite dehumanizing.
sentences.zh: 而且那些相当惨烈的外貌描写，也极具非人化色彩。

sentences.en: So the porters that you mentioned, you know, the people who are with the, they're carrying the stuff in their heads and they're chained together.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到的那些挑夫，你知道的，跟他们在一起的人，他们把东西顶在头上，还被铁链锁在一起。

sentences.en: They had the complete death-like indifference of unhappy savages or the railway workers dying in the grove.
sentences.zh: 他们带着一种不幸的野蛮人或是死在树林里的铁路工人那种彻底如死般的漠然。

sentences.en: Black shapes, black shadows of disease and starvation.
sentences.zh: 黑色的身形，疾病与饥饿的黑色阴影。

sentences.en: Would you talk like that about white European characters?
sentences.zh: 你会这样谈论白人欧洲角色吗？

sentences.en: I'm not entirely convinced that you would.
sentences.zh: 我可不怎么确信你会。

sentences.en: That I would accept.
sentences.zh: 这点我承认。

sentences.en: And we've already touched on Kurtz's African concubine, who is pure stereotyping.
sentences.zh: 而且我们刚才已经谈到库尔茨的那位非洲情妇了，那完全是刻板印象。

sentences.en: I mean, the pure kind of fantasy figure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，纯粹的那种幻想人物。

sentences.en: And I think that is where Conrad's kind of literary mastery falls down.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是康拉德的某种文学功底站不住脚的地方。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, first of all, there's a real complication here, which is that this isn't actually Conrad talking.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，首先，这里有一个很真实复杂的点，那就是这其实并不是康拉德在说话。

sentences.en: This is Marlowe talking.
sentences.zh: 这是马洛在说话。

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: Yes and no.
sentences.zh: 也不能完全这么说。

sentences.en: I mean, because there is a risk that you then start saying anything racist is Marlowe talking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，因为这会带来一种风险，你会开始把任何种族主义言论都当成是马洛在说。

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 并不是。

sentences.en: It's Conrad talking.
sentences.zh: 这是康拉德在说。

sentences.en: I mean, you can do it either way.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以从任何一个角度来解读。

sentences.en: I mean, if you start playing that game, depending on whether you want to get Conrad off the charge or not, you can fix your critique.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你开始玩这种把戏，取决于你是否想帮康拉德摆脱指控，你可以随心所欲地修正你的批判。

sentences.en: You can, but I think you have to.
sentences.zh: 你可以这么做，但我认为你不得不这么做。

sentences.en: So Achibi basically says in his lecture, I'm going to just basically treat Marlowe as if he's Conrad.
sentences.zh: 所以阿奇贝基本上在他的演讲中说，我打算直接把马洛当成康拉德来对待。

sentences.en: But Marlowe isn't Conrad.
sentences.zh: 但马洛并不是康拉德。

sentences.en: Conrad is the character listening to Marlowe, if Conrad is in the story at all.
sentences.zh: 如果康拉德真的存在于故事中的话，他才是那个听马洛讲述的角色。

sentences.en: So I think you just have to be a bit careful by always assuming that an author and their main character are the same person.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，你不能总是理所当然地认为作者和他们的主角是同一个人，还是得稍微谨慎一点。

sentences.en: Well, you notice this very, very powerfully when Marlowe is coming back and he's puzzling over Kurtz's character and what he represents.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当你注意到马洛回来时，他在琢磨库尔茨的性格以及他代表了什么，这种感觉就会非常非常强烈。

sentences.en: You have the sense that Marlowe is wrestling all the time.
sentences.zh: 你会有一种马洛一直在进行内心挣扎的感觉。

sentences.en: He's groping after truth, but there's always the sense that it's kind of slipping his fingers.
sentences.zh: 他在摸索真相，但你总会觉得真相从他的指缝间溜走。

sentences.en: And clearly, you know, he's grasping after the secrets of the human condition, but he is also grasping after the reality and the truth of what is going on in the Belgian Congo.
sentences.zh: 显然，你知道的，他在探寻人类境况的秘密，但他同时也在探寻比属刚果正在发生的事情的现实与真相。

sentences.en: And as we've said, this is written before Marlowe starts his kind of forensic examination of the details of what has been happening.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，写这段的时候，马洛还没有开始对正在发生的事情的细节进行那种抽丝剥茧的审视。

sentences.en: And you could say that there's an element there of the difficulty that historians have in making sense of what's been going on.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，这其中包含了一种历史学家在理解所发生的事情时所面临的困难。

sentences.en: And it is noticeable that we don't have African accounts of what happened.
sentences.zh: 而且值得注意的是，我们并没有关于所发生事情的非洲视角的记录。

sentences.en: I mean, this has been a problem that you've been acknowledging throughout our account, that it really is a story about what Europeans get up to rather than Africans.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是你在我们整个探讨过程中一直承认的一个问题，这实际上是一个关于欧洲人干了什么的故事，而不是关于非洲人的故事。

sentences.en: And I suppose that, you know, Conrad could talk to the Europeans, but he couldn't talk to the Africans.
sentences.zh: 我想你知道的，康拉德可以跟欧洲人对话，但他无法跟非洲人对话。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是对的。

sentences.en: Now, actually, ultimately, I think this question about is it a racist book or is it not is actually quite a boring one.
sentences.zh: 现在，实际上，归根结底，我认为关于它是不是一本种族主义书籍这个问题其实相当无聊。

sentences.en: I don't think it's Conrad clearly.
sentences.zh: 显然我不认为这是康拉德的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, it's such a terribly cliched thing to say.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，说这种话实在是太陈词滥调了。

sentences.en: Conrad obviously is a man of his age.
sentences.zh: 康拉德显然是个时代的产物。

sentences.en: He reflects the assumptions that he has grown up with, both in Russian occupied, you know, Eastern Poland, Ukraine, and later on sailing around on British merchant ships.
sentences.zh: 他反映了他在成长过程中所接受的种种假设，无论是在俄国占领下的东波兰、乌克兰，还是后来在英国商船上四处航行时。

sentences.en: I mean, he's not, you know, he's not outside time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他不是，你知道的，他并非超脱于时代之外。

sentences.en: Of course, he has prejudices and assumptions of his own, and they are expressed in his writing.
sentences.zh: 当然，他有他自己的偏见和成见，这些都在他的写作中表露无遗。

sentences.en: But the overall effect of this book is obviously not a, I mean,
sentences.zh: 但这本书的整体效果显然不是，我的意思是，

sentences.en: it's a book that clearly makes you think really seriously about the moral issues of imperialism and the civilizing mission and colonialism and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 这是一本显然会让你极其严肃地思考帝国主义、文明使命、殖民主义等种种道德问题的书。

sentences.en: I mean, how can it not?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，怎么可能不是呢？

sentences.en: Morel, who devoted his entire life to combating Leopold's regime in the Congo, said of it that it is the most powerful thing ever written on the subject.
sentences.zh: 莫雷尔将毕生精力用于反对利奥波德在刚果的政权，他对此书评价道，这是关于这个主题所写过的最有力量的作品。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think that is true.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这是真的。

sentences.en: And I think that are reigning authors, because they fail to measure up to the ideological standards of 2024,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，仅仅因为过去的作家不符合2024年的意识形态标准就去审判他们，

sentences.en: is the least interesting approach to literature that you could possibly adopt.
sentences.zh: 这是你所能采取的对文学最不感兴趣的方法。

sentences.en: Couldn't agree more.
sentences.zh: 简直不能更赞同了。

sentences.en: I mean, whether or not, of course, Conrad may have been racially prejudiced.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不管怎样，康拉德当然有可能带有种族偏见。

sentences.en: I mean, he may mean, he may not have been.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他可能有，我的意思是，他可能也没有。

sentences.en: It's, as you say, it's actually, I think, an incredibly boring question, because this is such an interesting book, and there's so many more things to say about it.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这实际上是一个极其无聊的问题，因为这是一本如此有趣的书，关于它还有太多太多的话可说。

sentences.en: But the possibility that he might be, I think, is woven into the story.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，他可能带有这种偏见的可能性，已经编织进了故事之中。

sentences.en: I think that might be, you know, the heart of darkness.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能就是，你知道的，黑暗之心。

sentences.en: That might be the horror.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是那种恐怖。

sentences.en: Conrad, Marlowe, whoever it is, is Conrad's voice within the heart of darkness.
sentences.zh: 康拉德、马洛，无论他是谁，都是黑暗之心内属于康拉德的声音。

sentences.en: I mean, all those people, I think, are implicated in what is being discussed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有这些人，我认为都卷入了正在讨论的事情中。

sentences.en: And I think that, going beyond that, the lasting appeal of the book is obviously it's about more than the Belgian Congo.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，除此之外，这本书持久的吸引力显然在于它不仅仅关乎比属刚果。

sentences.en: It's about more than King Leopold's free state or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅关乎利奥波德国王的自由邦或诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: To me, the key line in the book is actually that line that we quoted earlier, right at the beginning, before they even got to the Congo,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，书中关键的一行其实就是我们之前引用的那句，就在刚开头，甚至在他们到达刚果之前，

sentences.en: where Marlowe says to the people on the boat, and this also has been one of the dark places of the earth, and he's talking there about England.
sentences.zh: 马洛对船上的人说，这里也是地球上的黑暗之地之一，他当时指的是英国。

sentences.en: He's not talking about the Congo, and the darkness is there even before the steamboat has started its journey up the river, i.e. the darkness is not in the Congo.
sentences.zh: 他指的不是刚果，而且早在汽船开始逆流而上之前，黑暗就已经在那里了，也就是说，黑暗不在刚果。

sentences.en: It's not even in England.
sentences.zh: 它甚至不在英国。

sentences.en: It's in humanity.
sentences.zh: 它在人性中。

sentences.en: It's the human soul.
sentences.zh: 它在人类的灵魂里。

sentences.en: That's what I think the book's about.
sentences.zh: 这就是我认为这本书所讲述的内容。

sentences.en: And he's riffing there on the tendency, well, Stanley is always doing it, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他在那儿调侃那种倾向，好吧，斯坦利不一直是这样吗？

sentences.en: All his kind of massive volumes, he's always referring to darkest Africa.
sentences.zh: 他所有的那些皇皇巨著，总是动不动就提到黑暗的非洲。

sentences.en: That is the pivot, that London is one of the dark places, that the Thames Estuary was one of the dark places.
sentences.zh: 这就是核心所在，伦敦是黑暗之地之一，泰晤士河口也是黑暗之地之一。

sentences.en: And of course, dark has all these kind of rich shades of meaning.
sentences.zh: 当然，“黑暗”这个词有着各种丰富深层的含义。

sentences.en: And it may be that one of those shades of meaning could be cast as racist, but it is only one of them.
sentences.zh: 也许其中一种含义可以被解读为种族主义，但这只是其中之一。

sentences.en: And the racism that Europeans display towards Africans is also part of the racism that is being displayed by Romans towards the Britons.
sentences.zh: 欧洲人对非洲人表现出的种族主义，也是罗马人对不列颠人表现出的种族主义的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That this is what imperialists do.
sentences.zh: 这就是帝国主义者所做的事。

sentences.en: And I don't think it's even that he thinks this is what imperialists do.
sentences.zh: 而且我不认为这仅仅是他认为这是帝国主义者所做的事。

sentences.en: I think it's what human beings do.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是人类所做的事。

sentences.en: Conrad had a remarkably, I find it very attractive because I share it, a remarkably bleak view of human nature.
sentences.zh: 康拉德对人性有一种极其——我觉得很有吸引力，因为我也这么看——极其阴暗冷酷的看法。

sentences.en: In his letters to his friend Cunningham Graham, the SMP bloke that we mentioned earlier, he says of mankind, the year before he wrote Heart of Darkness,
sentences.zh: 在他写给朋友坎宁安·格雷姆的信中，也就是我们前面提到过的那个苏格兰民族党家伙，在写《黑暗之心》的前一年，他谈到人类时说，

sentences.en: he wrote to Cunningham Graham, he said,
sentences.zh: 他写信给坎宁安·格雷姆说：

sentences.en: Mankind is silly and cowardly, a wretched gang.
sentences.zh: 人类又愚蠢又懦弱，是一群可悲的家伙。

sentences.en: We're born initiated and succeeding generations clutch the inheritance of fear and brutality without a thought.
sentences.zh: 我们生来懵懂，后代则毫不思索地承袭了恐惧与残酷的遗产。

sentences.en: And another letter, he said, people go on, he said, about honour, justice, compassion, but nobody really believes in them.
sentences.zh: 在另一封信中，他说，人们总是喋喋不休地谈论荣誉、正义、同情，但根本没有人真正相信这些。

sentences.en: People believe only in, and I quote, gain, personal advantage, satisfied vanity, and words vanish and nothing remains, absolutely nothing, only a drop of mud, cold mud, dead mud,
sentences.zh: 人们只相信，我引用原话，“利益、个人好处、得到满足的虚荣”，而语言转瞬即逝，什么也没有留下，绝对什么也没有，只有一滴泥，冰冷的泥，死寂的泥，

sentences.en: launched in black space, turning round an extinguished sun.
sentences.zh: 被抛掷在黑暗的太空中，围绕着一颗熄灭的太阳旋转。

sentences.en: I love those lines.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这些台词了。

sentences.en: Conrad has a view of mankind, of human beings that is unbelievably sceptical, ironic, bleak, dark.
sentences.zh: 康拉德对人类、对个人的看法是难以置信地怀疑、讽刺、阴暗、冷酷。

sentences.en: Conservative.
sentences.zh: 保守。

sentences.en: Yeah, conservative.
sentences.zh: 对，保守。

sentences.en: I mean, he's sceptical about notions of progress and that Jerusalem can be built on the earth, definitely.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他对进步的概念以及耶路撒冷可以在大地上建立这种想法持怀疑态度，这是肯定的。

sentences.en: But I think the interesting thing about that is it's not just temperamental, but it's of his time.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有趣的是，这不仅是他的性格使然，也是他那个时代特有的。

sentences.en: Because I was thinking about the literature of the 1880s, 1890s.
sentences.zh: 因为我在回想1880年代、1890年代的文学。

sentences.en: So in 1890, the year he went to the Congo, one of my favourite books, La Bête Humaine by Émile Zola, which is about basically, I know it sounds very unpromising,
sentences.zh: 所以在1890年，他去刚果的那一年，我最喜欢的书之一，埃米尔·左拉的《人的兽性》，它基本上是关于——我知道这听起来很不着边际——

sentences.en: it's about a Parisian train driver who turns out to be a sex-crazed, homicidal maniac.
sentences.zh: 讲的是一个巴黎火车司机，结果却是一个性欲狂热、有杀人倾向的疯子。

sentences.en: He published this book and it's basically about the evil that is lurking within us all.
sentences.zh: 他出版这本书，基本上就是为了探讨潜藏在我们每个人内心的邪恶。

sentences.en: You know, even the most banal person is actually deep down.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，甚至连最平庸的人，其实在内心深处。

sentences.en: You know, we could all be serial killers and rapists and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们所有人都可能是连环杀手、强奸犯之类的人。

sentences.en: This is such a popular idea in very late Victorian culture.
sentences.zh: 这在维多利亚时代末期的文化中是一个非常受欢迎的想法。

sentences.en: Well, also with Dracula, which is published in 1897.
sentences.zh: 还有1897年出版的《吸血鬼德古拉》。

sentences.en: The idea of darkness coming to England.
sentences.zh: 黑暗降临英国的想法。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Or 1899, the same year Conrad publishes Heart of Darkness.
sentences.zh: 或者是1899年，也就是康拉德出版《黑暗之心》的同一年。

sentences.en: That's the year that Freud publishes The Interpretation of DreaMs.
sentences.zh: 那是弗洛伊德出版《梦的解析》的一年。

sentences.en: The idea that buried deep down in this kind of very primal and unfathomable way are anxieties and ghosts and terrible urges that we try to repress in our kind of civilised daily lives,
sentences.zh: 那种深深埋藏在某种极其原始且深不可测的方式之中的焦虑、幽灵和可怕的冲动，我们在文明的日常生活中试图压抑它们，

sentences.en: but will always come to claim us at night.
sentences.zh: 但它们总会在夜里前来索命。

sentences.en: I mean, again, all of this sort of stuff is simmering away in the European imagination at the time that Conrad is writing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，再次说明，所有这些东西在康拉德写作时期的欧洲人的想象力中都在暗流涌动。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no question that Heart of Darkness has given to very committed anti-racists, anti-imperialists, some of its language.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，毫无疑问，《黑暗之心》为那些坚定的反种族主义者、反帝国主义者提供了一些他们的话语表达。

sentences.en: So there was, I think, I can't remember, was it Netflix or something?
sentences.zh: 所以，我想我不记得了，是网飞还是别的什么？

sentences.en: There was a documentary series called Exterminate All the Brutes came out three, two or three years ago.
sentences.zh: 两三年前出过一部名为《灭绝群兽》的纪录片系列。

sentences.en: And it was about European colonialism and was not favourable at all.
sentences.zh: 它是关于欧洲殖民主义的，一点也不友善。

sentences.en: And it was based on a book by Sven Lindqvist, who is a Norwegian writer, who is absolutely excoriating about imperialism, particularly British imperialism.
sentences.zh: 它是基于挪威作家斯文·林德qvist的一本书改编的，他对帝国主义、尤其是英国帝国主义进行了极其严厉的鞭挞。

sentences.en: And of course, that title is coming from Kurtz's phrase, which in turn is written by Conrad.
sentences.zh: 当然，这个书名来自库尔茨的台词，而那句台词又是康拉德写的。

sentences.en: And so the echoes are very complex, I think, the kind of the ripples, the reverberations.
sentences.zh: 所以这些回响非常复杂，我认为，那种涟漪，那种共鸣。

sentences.en: I think to condemn it as a racist book is harsh, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为仅仅因为它是一本种族主义书籍而谴责它，未免太苛刻了。

sentences.en: I think it's not just harsh.
sentences.zh: 我认为这不仅仅是苛刻。

sentences.en: I think it's a total waste of time.
sentences.zh: 我认为这完全是在浪费时间。

sentences.en: I think it's a complete and utter waste of time when the book is so rich.
sentences.zh: 当这本书如此丰富时，我认为这完全是彻头彻尾的浪费时间。

sentences.en: And we've talked for too long.
sentences.zh: 而且我们聊得太久了。

sentences.en: And actually, we shouldn't, we're not in the business of preaching to listeners.
sentences.zh: 其实，我们不应该，我们的职责不是向听众说教。

sentences.en: Listeners can make up their own minds.
sentences.zh: 听众可以自己做出判断。

sentences.en: They should read the book.
sentences.zh: 他们应该去读这本书。

sentences.en: If you think it's racist, great.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得它是种族主义的，很好。

sentences.en: Crack on.
sentences.zh: 请便。

sentences.en: If you don't, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 如果你不觉得，太棒了。

sentences.en: Tom, why don't we end with the end of the book?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们为什么不以这本书的结尾来收尾呢？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Malu ceased and sat apart, indistinct and silent in the pose of a meditating Buddha.
sentences.zh: 马洛停了下来，坐在一旁，在一片模糊中沉默着，摆出一副沉思的佛陀姿态。

sentences.en: Nobody moved for a time.
sentences.zh: 有一会儿谁也没有动。

sentences.en: We've lost the first of the ebb, said the director suddenly.
sentences.zh: 我们错过了退潮的第一波，导演突然说道。

sentences.en: I raised my head.
sentences.zh: 我抬起头。

sentences.en: The offing was barred by a black bank of clouds.
sentences.zh: 远处的洋面上横亘着一岸黑色的云墙。

sentences.en: And the tranquil waterway leading to the uttermost ends of the earth flowed sombre under an overcast sky.
sentences.zh: 那条通往世界尽头的宁静水道在阴沉的天空下显得阴暗莫测。

sentences.en: Seemed to lead into the heart of an immense darkness.
sentences.zh: 似乎通向一片无垠黑暗的核心。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
